title: Physics on arXiv — Monday, 5 October 2026: 8 notable papers
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This is an inferred selection, not a popularity ranking; citation evidence is sparse or unavailable for most newly announced papers.

sections.title: First observation of electron antineutrinos from nuclear reactors at Super-Kamiokande
sections.abstract: Using 411.52 live days of gadolinium-enhanced Super-Kamiokande data, the collaboration reports a reactor-antineutrino signal at about 6σ and fits solar-neutrino oscillation parameters jointly with the reactor sample.
sections.claimed_result: The authors disfavor the no-reactor hypothesis at approximately 6σ and report a combined solar-plus-reactor fit of sin²θ₁₂ = 0.332 (+0.028/−0.026) and Δm²₂₁ = (8.94 ± about 0.47) × 10⁻⁵ eV².
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 411.52 live days from Super-Kamiokande’s SK-Gd phase, with accidental, geoneutrino, and spallation backgrounds considered.
sections.unique_caveat: The reactor-only and solar-neutrino samples are statistically compatible at only 1.9σ in the paper’s comparison, and the exposure is finite; the preprint is submitted to Physical Review Letters.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Concrete detector-level observation with a reported ~6σ signal and oscillation fit; independently surfaced in a researcher’s 5 October arXiv-picks list. This supports notice, not a measured readership lead.

sections.title: Low-Overhead Quantum Error Correction with Boundary-Connected Planar Modules
sections.abstract: The authors propose modular hyperbolic surface and color codes using sparse static connections between planar processor modules, with circuit-level simulations indicating much lower physical-qubit overhead than surface-code memories.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say their modular memory design can lower qubit overhead while maintaining fault tolerance, and give projected code parameters including encoding rate k/n = 1/16 and distance d ≥ 22.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; circuit-level simulations using modular syndrome extraction plus neural-network and matching decoders.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline resource gains are simulation results and larger-system projections, not a demonstrated hardware implementation; performance depends on the modeled inter-module seam errors and decoder assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports circuit-level simulation results of 10× or greater overhead reduction and a projected >30× reduction for larger codes on a central fault-tolerance bottleneck; technical-significance signal, not readership evidence.

sections.title: Multi-Band Constraints on Cosmic Strings: Unifying Harmonic and Burst Spectra
sections.abstract: The authors unify two descriptions of gravitational waves from cosmic-string loops and use joint PTA and LVK data to constrain string tension and loop-model parameters.
sections.claimed_result: Across four representative loop-distribution models, the authors find that a harmonic treatment strengthens LVK bounds by 21–31% in three models, which then cannot explain the PTA common signal; one model remains viable under their joint analysis.
sections.evidence_type: Observational-data analysis and theoretical modeling; joint Bayesian inference using NANOGrav, EPTA, and LVK datasets with four loop-distribution models.
sections.unique_caveat: Conclusions depend on assumed cosmic-string loop distributions and radiation parameters; different models yield different outcomes, so the PTA signal is not established as cosmic-string evidence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Connects three physics archives, combines NANOGrav, EPTA, and LVK data, and has report number LIGO-P2600521-v1; cross-field, data-linked relevance.

sections.title: Dark Energy Survey Year 6 Results: fast and interpretable posterior predictive checks for correlated cosmic probes
sections.abstract: The DES collaboration introduces a fast posterior-predictive consistency diagnostic for correlated cosmological probes, tests it on DES Year 3 data and simulations, and describes its role in DES Year 6 validation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors’ scalar ΔPPD statistic reproduces the same inter-probe tensions identified by calibrated DES Year 3 tests, runs in minutes per test, and responds to injected inconsistency in simulated Year 6 analyses.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; Gaussian-mixture approximation, DES Year 3 measurements, toy models, and simulated DES Year 6 noise realizations.
sections.unique_caveat: Nuisance-parameter shifts can hide tensions, while weakly constrained parameter directions can create apparent tension between otherwise consistent probes; the authors advise using ΔPPD alongside other checks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Major survey collaboration validation method with public code, listed on the DES Year 6 cosmology-results page and tested against published DES Year 3 tension results and simulated Year 6 analyses.

sections.title: Third-Order Logarithmic Resummation for Jet-Vetoed Higgs Production
sections.abstract: The authors present a third-logarithmic-order QCD prediction for jet-vetoed Higgs production, combining a next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order calculation with next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-logarithmic resummation.
sections.claimed_result: At representative veto scales near 30 GeV and jet radius R = 0.4, the authors report an approximately 3% increase over the fixed-order prediction and residual perturbative uncertainty of about 3% after resummation.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; high-order perturbative QCD calculation and logarithmic resummation for LHC Higgs production.
sections.unique_caveat: The quoted uncertainty is residual perturbative uncertainty, not the total experimental or modeling uncertainty; the prediction remains tied to the specified veto scale and jet definition.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Claims a first-in-class precision calculation for a standard LHC Higgs observable, cross-listed between phenomenology and experiment; CERN report CERN-TH-2026-173.

sections.title: Complex-momentum form factors from lattice QCD
sections.abstract: The authors propose obtaining form factors at complex momenta directly from Euclidean position-space correlators using a bilateral Laplace transform, and test the method in a two-dimensional O(3) model.
sections.claimed_result: For the pion form factor, the authors derive access to complex Q² where Re(Q²) > −4m_π² without analytically continuing the correlator or solving an inverse problem.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational; derivation for infinite-volume correlators, proposed finite-volume estimators, and Monte Carlo tests in the two-dimensional O(3) nonlinear sigma model.
sections.unique_caveat: The numerical test is in the O(3) model, not a realistic finite-volume QCD calculation; the paper discusses but does not establish which finite-volume estimator will work best in production lattice studies.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Method addresses analytic-continuation and inverse-problem difficulties, cross-lists lattice and theoretical high-energy physics, and includes a Monte Carlo test in a field theory.

sections.title: Guide field effects on particle acceleration in three-dimensional relativistic magnetic reconnection
sections.abstract: Three-dimensional pair-plasma simulations indicate that the fast particle-acceleration channel persists as guide fields strengthen, but involves fewer particles and yields steeper spectra and lower maximum energies.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find the fast acceleration channel absent in 2D but persistent in their 3D runs across the guide fields studied; increasing the guide field reduces the accelerated fraction, steepens spectra, and lowers maximum Lorentz factors.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; 3D relativistic pair-plasma particle-in-cell simulations, complemented by 2D runs with open outflow boundaries.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a simulation result for the modeled pair-plasma setup, not a direct measurement of astrophysical particle spectra; extrapolation depends on how well the simulated regime represents real sources.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-lists astrophysics and plasma physics and compares 3D with 2D simulations across guide-field strengths, testing robustness of an acceleration mechanism relevant to high-energy astrophysical plasmas.

sections.title: Higgsino dark matter compatible with the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy nuclear-recoil event and IceCube constraints
sections.abstract: The authors test whether inelastic Higgsino dark matter can explain an LZ high-energy recoil event while remaining consistent with IceCube limits, finding allowed regions that vary strongly with astrophysical and solar-cooling assumptions.
sections.claimed_result: Under selected halo, solar-cooling, and sideband assumptions, the authors find Higgsino parameter regions compatible with the LZ event and IceCube null searches, spanning roughly 2 TeV to hundreds of TeV or more.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; likelihood analysis of the LZ event and IceCube constraints under alternative halo and solar-cooling assumptions.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a proposed explanation of a single event, not a detection; compatibility changes with the high-speed halo tail, solar cooling model, and whether the LZ sideband constraint is included.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Directly connects a reported LZ event to IceCube constraints and cross-lists particle phenomenology, cosmology, and theory; timely testable interpretation, not evidence of detection.
